subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Synthetic Biology: Designing Life From Scratch
description: A quick win: understand Synthetic Biology: Designing Life From Scratch.

hook.text: In 2010, Craig Venter created the first synthetic cell. Its entire genome was designed on a computer and assembled chemically.

buildup.text: Synthetic biology treats DNA like programming code. Standardized parts — BioBricks — snap together like software modules.

discovery.text: Engineered yeast already produces insulin, antimalarial drugs, and spider silk. Biology becomes a manufacturing platform.

twist.text: Biosecurity is a concern. The same tools that make medicines could create dangerous pathogens. Dual-use risk is real.

climax.text: The iGEM competition has thousands of students building synthetic organisms yearly. A generation is learning to engineer biology.

punchline.text: Design a genome. Build it. Boot up a living cell. Biology is now engineering.

quiz.question: What are BioBricks in synthetic biology?
options: Tiny building blocks of protein used to construct synthetic cell walls
Standardized DNA parts that snap together like software modules to build genetic circuits
Biodegradable bricks made from engineered bacteria for sustainable construction
